newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DTC sales start slowly in Dutch money market.
newsitem.headline: DTC sales start slowly in Dutch money market.

text.p: Trade in a new batch of Dutch Treasury Certificates (DTCs) got off to a slow start on Monday as the Finance Ministry opened three new DTC programmes.
The new DTCs have maturity dates of January 2, February 28 and March 27, in 1997. Each programme has a maximum issue amount of 7.5 billion guilders.
The new programmes will partially replace two outstanding programmes, which mature on October 31 and November 29.
But the facility will also cover a gap left by an absence of Dutch government bond issues in the final quarter of 1996.
The Finance ministry said it had covered 33.3 billion guilders of its 35.1 billion borrowing requirement for 1996.
Dealers said the rate for the new DTCs had to go up somewhat before the certificates would attract more buying interest.
Dealers cited rates of 2.77 percent for the February and March contracts.
"This is just a little too low," said one dealer, adding that DTCs had the advantage of being a very liquid money market instrument.
The first settlements are set for October 21, 1996.
The Finance Ministry's capital markets agency is authorised to repurchase the DTCs once they have been issued and may resell them once they have been repurchased.

Dealers said overall business in the money market was a little more lively as a result of the new DTC programmes and the start of position-squaring by money market players as the last quarter of the year gets under way.
"I noted some business in three-month deposits," said one dealer.
The trend in rates was slightly lower, dealers said. "Long-dated deposits could come down a touch further," said one.
One-year deposits were bid at 2.96 on Monday versus 2.98 just before the weekend. Call money edged down a few basis points, trading between 2.56 and 2.62 percent bid.
Dealers foresee no change in the special advances rate this afternoon when the central bank sets a new pact at 1400 GMT.
The guilder was slightly weaker against the mark at 112.2050 per 100 marks from 112.195 on Friday.
